sentences.zh: 昔自在古，歷建正作於孟春。

translations.literal: In ancient times, the proper beginning of the calendar was fixed in the first month of spring.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, the calendar was set to begin in the first month of spring.

sentences.zh: 於時冰泮發蟄，百草奮興，秭鳺先滜。

translations.literal: At that time the ice melts and the hibernating creatures stir, the hundred grasses flourish, and the cuckoo is first to call.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, the ice melts and the hibernating creatures stir; the hundred grasses flourish, and the cuckoo calls first.

sentences.zh: 物乃歲具，生於東，次順四時，卒于冬分。

translations.literal: Things then complete the year, spring from the east, follow the four seasons in order, and end at the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Things then complete the year, springing from the east, moving in order through the four seasons, and ending at the winter solstice.

translations.literal: When the rooster crows three times, dawn arrives.
translations.idiomatic: At the third crowing of the rooster, daylight finally arrives.

translations.literal: It runs through the twelve monthly divisions and ends in Chou.
translations.idiomatic: It passes through the twelve monthly nodes and comes to completion at Chou.

translations.literal: When the sun and moon are complete, there is brightness.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun and moon are in order, brightness results.

sentences.zh: 明者孟也，幽者幼也，幽明者雌雄也。

translations.literal: Bright means the elder; dark means the younger. Dark and bright together mean female and male.
translations.idiomatic: Bright means the elder; dark means the younger. Together, dark and bright mean female and male.

sentences.zh: 雌雄代興，而順至正之統也。

translations.literal: Female and male alternate in succession, thus following the right order.
translations.idiomatic: Female and male rise in alternation, following the proper succession of the correct order.

translations.literal: The sun returns to the west and rises in the east.
translations.idiomatic: The sun returns to the west, then brings light forth in the east;

translations.literal: The moon returns to the east and rises in the west.
translations.idiomatic: the moon returns to the east, then brings light forth in the west.

sentences.zh: 正不率天，又不由人，則凡事易壞而難成矣。

translations.literal: If the calendar does not follow heaven or derive from human ordering, then all affairs are easy to ruin and hard to complete.
translations.idiomatic: If the calendar neither follows Heaven nor rests on human ordering, then every undertaking becomes easy to ruin and difficult to complete.

sentences.zh: 王者易姓受命，必慎始初，改正朔，易服色，推本天元，順承厥意。

translations.literal: When rulers change their surname and receive the mandate, they must be cautious at the beginning, reform the calendar’s starting point, change the colors of dress, trace back to the root of the heavenly origin, and follow its intention.
translations.idiomatic: When rulers change their surname and receive the mandate, they must take care over the beginning, reform the calendar’s starting point, change the colors of dress, trace back to the heavenly origin, and follow its intent.

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：神農以前尚矣。

translations.literal: The Grand Historian says: the age before Shennong lies far back in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian says: the age before Shennong is remote antiquity indeed.

sentences.zh: 蓋黃帝考定星歷，建立五行，起消息，正閏餘，於是有天地神祇物類之官，是謂五官。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor examined and fixed the star calendar, established the five phases, initiated the waxing and waning, and corrected intercalary remainders. Thereupon there were officials for heaven, earth, spirits, and things and categories; these are called the five officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor examined and fixed the stellar calendar, established the five phases, set the cycles of waxing and waning in motion, and corrected intercalary remainders. There were then officials for heaven, earth, spirits, and the categories of things; these were called the five officials.

translations.literal: Each administered its own sequence and did not disturb the others.
translations.idiomatic: Each kept charge of its own sequence, and they did not throw one another into disorder.

sentences.zh: 民是以能有信，神是以能有明德。

translations.literal: Thus, the people were able to trust, and the spirits were able to have bright virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, the people could have trust, and the spirits could manifest bright virtue.

sentences.zh: 民神異業，敬而不瀆，故神降之嘉生，民以物享，災禍不生，所求不匱。

translations.literal: People and spirits had different occupations; when respectful and not profane, the spirits bestowed auspicious births, the people enjoyed the things they offered, disasters did not arise, and what they sought was not lacking.
translations.idiomatic: People and spirits had separate duties. When the people were reverent and did not profane them, the spirits bestowed auspicious growth, the people enjoyed the things they offered, disasters did not arise, and what they sought was not lacking.

sentences.zh: 少暤氏之衰也，九黎亂德，民神雜擾，不可放物，禍菑薦至，莫盡其氣。

translations.literal: When the Shaohao clan declined, the Nine Li brought virtue into disorder. People and spirits were thrown into confusion; things could not be properly released; disasters and calamities came repeatedly, and none could exhaust their qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shaohao clan declined, the Nine Li threw virtue into disorder. People and spirits were mixed together in confusion; things could not be properly regulated; disasters and calamities came repeatedly, and none could fully express their vital force.

sentences.zh: 顓頊受之，乃命南正重司天以屬神，命火正黎司地以屬民，使復舊常，無相侵瀆。

translations.literal: Zhuanxu received it and ordered Chong, the Southern Corrector, to govern heaven and be attached to the spirits, and ordered Li, the Fire Corrector, to govern earth and be attached to the people, so that he restored the old constant and there was no mutual invasion or profanation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanxu inherited this situation and ordered Chong, the Southern Corrector, to govern heaven and attend to the spirits, and Li, the Fire Corrector, to govern earth and attend to the people. In this way he restored the old order, so that neither side invaded or profaned the other.

sentences.zh: 其後三苗服九黎之德，故二官咸廢所職，而閏餘乖次，孟陬殄滅，攝提無紀，歷數失序。

translations.literal: Afterward, the Three Miao followed the virtue of the Nine Li, so the two officials both abandoned their duties, and the intercalary remainder was out of sequence, the first month was extinguished, Sheti was unrecorded, and the calendar numbers lost their order.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, the Three Miao followed the disordered ways of the Nine Li, so the two officials both abandoned their duties. The intercalary remainder fell out of sequence, the first month was obliterated, Sheti went unrecorded, and the calendrical numbers lost their order.

sentences.zh: 堯復遂重黎之後，不忘舊者，使復典之，而立羲和之官。

translations.literal: Yao in turn continued the descendants of Chong and Li, not forgetting the old order, and again made them administer it, establishing the office of Xi and He.
translations.idiomatic: Yao in turn restored the descendants of Chong and Li, not forgetting the old order, and again made them administer it, establishing the offices of Xi and He.

sentences.zh: 明時正度，則陰陽調，風雨節，茂氣至，民無夭疫。

translations.literal: When the bright measure is established in due time, yin and yang are harmonized, wind and rain are in season, luxuriant qi arrives, and the people suffer no untimely epidemics.
translations.idiomatic: When the seasons are clearly measured and the standards are correct, yin and yang are harmonized, wind and rain come in season, flourishing qi arrives, and the people suffer no untimely epidemics.

sentences.zh: 年耆禪舜，申戒文祖，云「天之歷數在爾躬」。

translations.literal: When he was old in years, he yielded the throne to Shun and again earnestly admonished at the Wen ancestral shrine, saying, “The calendar numbers of Heaven are in your person.”
translations.idiomatic: When he grew old, he yielded the throne to Shun and again earnestly instructed at the Wen ancestral shrine, saying, “The calendrical mandate of Heaven rests upon you.”

translations.literal: Shun likewise passed this command to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Shun likewise passed this command to Yu.

translations.literal: From this we see how much kings valued it.
translations.idiomatic: From this one can see how heavily kings valued the calendar.

sentences.zh: 夏正以正月，殷正以十二月，周正以十一月。

translations.literal: The Xia calendar took the first month as its beginning, the Yin calendar the twelfth month, and the Zhou calendar the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia calendar began with the first month, the Yin calendar with the twelfth, and the Zhou calendar with the eleventh.

sentences.zh: 蓋三王之正若循環，窮則反本。

translations.literal: Indeed, the three kings’ calendars revolved in a cycle, returning to their root when the cycle was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, the calendars of the Three Kings moved in a cycle, returning to their root when the cycle was exhausted.

translations.literal: When the realm has the Way, it does not lose its sequence and order.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm possesses the Way, it does not lose its calendrical sequence and order;

sentences.zh: 無道，則正朔不行於諸侯。

translations.literal: Without the Way, the correct calendar does not prevail among the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: when it lacks the Way, the proper calendar and first day of the month do not circulate among the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 幽、厲之後，周室微，陪臣執政，史不記時，君不告朔，故疇人子弟分散，或在諸夏，或在夷狄，是以其禨祥廢而不統。

translations.literal: After the reigns of You and Li, the Zhou house declined; subordinate ministers seized power; historians did not record the seasons; lords did not report the new moon. Thus, the descendants of the calendar experts scattered, some among the various Xia states and some among the Yi and Di, so their auspicious observations fell into disuse and lost their system.
translations.idiomatic: After the reigns of Kings You and Li, the Zhou house declined; subordinate ministers seized power; historians did not record the seasons; lords did not announce the new moon. Thus, the descendants of the calendar experts scattered, some among the various Xia states and some among the Yi and Di, so their omen observations fell into disuse and lost their system.

sentences.zh: 周襄王二十六年閏三月，而春秋非之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of King Xiang of Zhou, there was an intercalary third month, which the Spring and Autumn Annals condemned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of King Xiang of Zhou, there was an intercalary third month, which the Spring and Autumn Annals criticized.

sentences.zh: 先王之正時也，履端於始，舉正於中，歸邪於終。

translations.literal: The former kings’ regulation of time was to set the beginning at the start, establish the correct point in the middle, and return what was askew at the end.
translations.idiomatic: The former kings’ regulation of time set the beginning at the start, established the correct point in the middle, and brought what was askew back into order at the end.

translations.literal: If the beginning is properly set at the start, the sequence does not err;
translations.idiomatic: Set the starting point correctly at the beginning, and the sequence will not go astray;

translations.literal: if the correct point is established in the middle, the people are not confused;
translations.idiomatic: raise the correct standard at the center, and the people will not be confused;

translations.literal: if what is askew is returned at the end, affairs are not opposed.
translations.idiomatic: if what is askew is brought back into order at the end, affairs do not go awry.

sentences.zh: 其後戰國并爭，在於彊國禽敵，救急解紛而已，豈遑念斯哉！

translations.literal: Afterward the Warring States contended with one another; they were occupied only with strong states capturing enemies and with emergency relief and untangling disputes. How could they have leisure for this?
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Warring States contended with one another; they were occupied only with strong states subduing enemies and with emergency relief and untangling disputes. How could they have leisure for this?

sentences.zh: 是時獨有鄒衍，明於五德之傳，而散消息之分，以顯諸侯。

translations.literal: At that time, only Zou Yan clearly understood the transmission of the Five Virtues and explained the divisions of waxing and waning, to display them to the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, only Zou Yan clearly understood the transmission of the Five Virtues and explained the divisions of waxing and waning, presenting them to the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 而亦因秦滅六國，兵戎極煩，又升至尊之日淺，未暇遑也。

translations.literal: And because Qin had destroyed the six states, military affairs were incessant and the days since his rise to supreme power were still few, he had no leisure for it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qin had destroyed the six states, military affairs were incessant, and only a short time had passed since its ruler rose to supreme power, he had no leisure for it.

sentences.zh: 而亦頗推五勝，而自以為獲水德之瑞，更名河曰「德水」，而正以十月，色上黑。

translations.literal: He also pushed the Five Conquests quite far, taking himself to have obtained the auspicious sign of water virtue, renamed the river “Virtue Water,” adopted the tenth month as the calendar’s beginning, and made black the principal color.
translations.idiomatic: He also pressed the theory of the Five Conquests quite far, taking himself to have obtained the auspicious sign of water virtue. He renamed the Yellow River “Virtue Water,” adopted the tenth month as the calendar’s beginning, and made black the principal color.

sentences.zh: 然歷度閏餘，未能睹其真也。

translations.literal: Yet in matters of calendrical measures and intercalary remainders, he did not reach the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in matters of calendrical measures and intercalary remainders, he did not grasp the truth.

sentences.zh: 漢興，高祖曰「北畤待我而起」，亦自以為獲水德之瑞。

translations.literal: When Han rose, Gaozu said, “The northern altar awaited me and rose with me,” and he also took himself to have received the auspicious sign of water virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Han rose, Gaozu said, “The northern altar waited for me before it arose,” and he too took himself to have received the auspicious sign of water virtue.

sentences.zh: 雖明習歷及張蒼等，咸以為然。

translations.literal: Even those who were skilled in the calendar, including Zhang Cang and others, all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Even Zhang Cang and the others who understood the calendar clearly all took this to be correct.

sentences.zh: 是時天下初定，方綱紀大基，高后女主，皆未遑，故襲秦正朔服色。

translations.literal: At that time the realm had only just been settled and the great foundation of order was being laid. Empress Gao, as a female ruler, had no leisure for it, so the Qin calendar, new moon, and clothing colors were retained.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the realm had only just been settled and the great foundation of order was being laid. Empress Gao, ruling as a woman, had no leisure for the matter, so the Qin calendar, monthly beginnings, and clothing colors were retained.

sentences.zh: 至孝文時，魯人公孫臣以終始五德上書，言「漢得土德，宜更元，改正朔，易服色。

translations.literal: When it came to Emperor Xiaowen, Lu Gongsun Chen memorialized on the succession of the Five Virtues, saying, “Han has obtained earth virtue. It should change the era, reform the calendar, and alter the clothing colors.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Emperor Xiaowen, Gongsun Chen of Lu memorialized on the succession of the Five Virtues, saying, “Han has obtained earth virtue. It should change the era, reform the calendar, and alter the clothing colors.

translations.literal: There should be an auspicious omen; the auspicious omen would be the appearance of a yellow dragon.”
translations.idiomatic: There ought to be an auspicious sign, and that sign would be a yellow dragon appearing."

sentences.zh: 事下丞相張蒼，張蒼亦學律歷，以為非是，罷之。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to Chancellor Zhang Cang, who had also studied the pitch-pipes and the calendar and judged it incorrect, so it was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to Chancellor Zhang Cang, who had also studied the pitch-pipes and calendar. He judged it incorrect, so it was dropped.

sentences.zh: 其後黃龍見成紀，張蒼自黜，所欲論著不成。

translations.literal: Later, a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji. Zhang Cang voluntarily resigned from office, and what he wished to set down and discuss did not come to fruition.
translations.idiomatic: Later, a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji. Zhang Cang resigned of his own accord, and what he had wished to compose and discuss never came to fruition.

sentences.zh: 而新垣平以望氣見，頗言正歷服色事，貴幸，後作亂，故孝文帝廢不復問。

translations.literal: Xinyuan Ping, who was known through his observations of qi, spoke extensively on reforming the calendar and clothing colors, and he was favored and honored. Later he caused disorder, so Emperor Wen discarded the matter and did not pursue it again.
translations.idiomatic: Xinyuan Ping, who became known through his observations of qi, spoke extensively on reforming the calendar and clothing colors, and he was favored and honored. Later he caused disorder, so Emperor Wen discarded the matter and did not pursue it again.

sentences.zh: 至今上即位，招致方士唐都，分其天部；

translations.literal: When the current emperor ascended the throne, he summoned the fangshi Tang Du and had him apportion the heavenly divisions;
translations.idiomatic: When the present emperor came to the throne, he summoned the fangshi Tang Du to divide the celestial sectors;

sentences.zh: 而巴落下閎運算轉歷，然後日辰之度與夏正同。

translations.literal: and when Luoxia Hong of Ba calculated the revolving calendar, the degrees of the sun and the days then matched the Xia calendar.
translations.idiomatic: then Luoxia Hong of Ba calculated the rotating calendar, and only afterward did the sun’s degrees and the days correspond with the Xia calendar.

translations.literal: He then changed the era name, altered the office titles, and sacrificed at Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then changed the era name, revised the official titles, and performed the Feng sacrifice at Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 因詔御史曰：「乃者，有司言星度之未定也，廣延宣問，以理星度，未能詹也。

translations.literal: He therefore issued an edict to the imperial secretary, saying: “Recently the relevant officials reported that the stellar degrees had not yet been fixed. I have widely extended inquiry to set right the stellar degrees, but have not yet fully attained clarity.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore issued an edict to the imperial secretary, saying: “Recently the relevant officials reported that the stellar degrees had not yet been fixed. I have widely extended inquiry to rectify the stellar degrees, but have not yet gained full clarity.

sentences.zh: 蓋聞昔者黃帝合而不死，名察度驗，定清濁，起五部，建氣物分數。

translations.literal: I have heard that in antiquity the Yellow Emperor attained unity and did not die; he named, examined, and verified the degrees, fixed the clear and turbid, established the five divisions, and set up the measures and proportions of qi and things.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in antiquity the Yellow Emperor joined with the Way and did not die; he named, examined, and verified the degrees, fixed the clear and the turbid, established the five divisions, and set up the numerical measures of qi and things.

translations.literal: But this is still very remote indeed.
translations.idiomatic: But this is still very remote indeed.

translations.literal: The records are incomplete and music has fallen into decay; I am deeply distressed by this.
translations.idiomatic: The records are incomplete and music has slackened into decay; this deeply grieves me.

sentences.zh: 朕唯未能循明也，紬績日分，率應水德之勝。

translations.literal: I alone have not yet been able to follow and clarify the way, but have only continued the daily divisions, broadly conforming to the predominance of water virtue.
translations.idiomatic: I alone have not yet been able to follow and clarify the established calendar, but have only carried forward the daily divisions, broadly conforming to the ascendancy of water virtue.

sentences.zh: 今日順夏至，黃鐘為宮，林鐘為徵，太蔟為商，南呂為羽，姑洗為角。

translations.literal: Today, in accordance with the summer solstice, Huangzhong is gong, Linzhong is zhi, Taicu is shang, Nanlü is yu, and Guxi is jue.
translations.idiomatic: Now, in accord with the summer solstice, Huangzhong serves as gong, Linzhong as zhi, Taicu as shang, Nanlu as yu, and Guxi as jue.

sentences.zh: 自是以後，氣復正，羽聲復清，名復正變，以至子日當冬至，則陰陽離合之道行焉。

translations.literal: From this point on, the qi again became correct, the yu pitch again became clear, and the names again returned to proper alteration. By the time the zi day coincides with the winter solstice, the way of yin and yang separating and joining is put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: From this point on, the qi again became correct, the yu pitch again became clear, and the names again returned to their proper alternation. When the zi day coincides with the winter solstice, the way of yin and yang separating and joining is put into practice.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲子朔旦冬至已詹，其更以七年為太初元年。

translations.literal: By the time the eleventh month, Jiazi, new moon, and winter solstice were all reached, they changed it so that the seventh year became the first year of Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: When the eleventh month, the jiazi day, the new moon, dawn, and the winter solstice all coincided, they changed the calendar so that the seventh year became the first year of Taichu.

sentences.zh: 年名『焉逢攝提格』，月名『畢聚』，日得甲子，夜半朔旦冬至。」

translations.literal: The year was named “Yanfeng Shetige”; the month was named “Biju”; the day was Jiazi; and at midnight came the new moon, dawn, and winter solstice.”
translations.idiomatic: The year was named “Yanfeng Shetige”; the month was named “Biju”; the day was Jiazi; and at midnight the new moon, dawn, and winter solstice coincided.”

sentences.zh: 歷術甲子篇太初元年，歲名「焉逢攝提格」，月名「畢聚」，日得甲子，夜半朔旦冬至。

translations.literal: The calendar method of the Jiazi chapter for the first year of Taichu: the year was named “Yanfeng Shetige”; the month was named “Biju”; the day obtained Jiazi; at midnight came the new moon, dawn, and winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar method of the Jiazi chapter for the first year of Taichu: the year was named “Yanfeng Shetige”; the month was named “Biju”; the day was Jiazi; at midnight the new moon, dawn, and winter solstice coincided.

sentences.zh: 正北十二無大餘，無小餘；

translations.literal: North twelve no large remainder, no small remainder;
translations.idiomatic: Northern alignment, regular year of 12 months: the large remainder is 0, and the small remainder is 0.

translations.literal: No large remainder, no small remainder;
translations.idiomatic: The large remainder is 0, and the small remainder is 0.

translations.literal: Yanfeng Shetige Tai Chu first year.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfeng Shetige, the first year of Taichu.

sentences.zh: 十二大餘五十四，小餘三百四十八；

translations.literal: Twelve large remainder fifty four, small remainder three hundred forty eight;
translations.idiomatic: Regular year, 12 months: the large remainder is 54, and the small remainder is 348.

translations.literal: Large remainder five, small remainder eight;
translations.idiomatic: The large remainder is 5, and the small remainder is 8.

translations.literal: Duameng Dan E second year.
translations.idiomatic: Duameng Dan E, the second year.

sentences.zh: 閏十三大餘四十八，小餘六百九十六；

translations.literal: Intercalary thirteen large remainder forty eight, small remainder six hundred ninety six;
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary year, 13 months: the large remainder is 48, and the small remainder is 696.

translations.literal: Large remainder ten, small remainder sixteen;
translations.idiomatic: The large remainder is 10, and the small remainder is 16.

translations.literal: You Zhao Zhi Xu third year.
translations.idiomatic: You Zhao Zhi Xu, the third year.

sentences.zh: 十二大餘十二，小餘六百三；

translations.literal: Twelve large remainder twelve, small remainder six hundred three;
translations.idiomatic: Regular year, 12 months: the large remainder is 12, and the small remainder is 603.

translations.literal: Large remainder fifteen, small remainder twenty four;
translations.idiomatic: The large remainder is 15, and the small remainder is 24.

translations.literal: Qiang Wu Da Huang Luo fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Wu Da Huang Luo, the fourth year.

translations.literal: Twelve large remainder seven, small remainder eleven;
translations.idiomatic: Regular year, 12 months: the large remainder is 7, and the small remainder is 11.

translations.literal: Large remainder twenty one, no small remainder;
translations.idiomatic: The large remainder is 21, and the small remainder is 0.

translations.literal: Tu Wei Dun Zang Tian Han first year.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Wei Dun Zang, the first year of Tianhan.

sentences.zh: 閏十三大餘一，小餘三百五十九；

translations.literal: Intercalary thirteen large remainder one, small remainder three hundred fifty nine;
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary year, 13 months: the large remainder is 1, and the small remainder is 359.

translations.literal: Large remainder twenty six, small remainder eight;
translations.idiomatic: The large remainder is 26, and the small remainder is 8.

translations.literal: Zhu Li Xie Qiao second year.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Li Xie Qiao, the second year.

sentences.zh: 十二大餘二十五，小餘二百六十六；

translations.literal: Twelve large remainder twenty five, small remainder two hundred sixty six;
translations.idiomatic: Regular year, 12 months: the large remainder is 25, and the small remainder is 266.

translations.literal: Large remainder thirty one, small remainder sixteen;
translations.idiomatic: The large remainder is 31, and the small remainder is 16.

translations.literal: Shang Heng Dun Tan third year.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Heng Dun Tan, the third year.

sentences.zh: 十二大餘十九，小餘六百一十四；

translations.literal: Twelve large remainder nineteen, small remainder six hundred fourteen;
translations.idiomatic: Regular year, 12 months: the large remainder is 19, and the small remainder is 614.

sentences.zh: 大餘三十六，小餘二十四；

translations.literal: Large remainder thirty six, small remainder twenty four;
translations.idiomatic: The large remainder is 36, and the small remainder is 24.

translations.literal: Zhao Yang Zuo E fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yang Zuo E, the fourth year.
